lines.speaker: kopi
lines.text: Good morning, Kracked Devs! It's Friday, October second. I'm Kopi, and here's what shipped in tech.

lines.speaker: kopi
lines.text: First up: the decision model craze. After Jev went viral, Amazon open-sourced Strands Decider, and Cloudflare launched Clef. They don't write text. They just pick an answer, with odds, in milliseconds.

lines.speaker: kopi
lines.text: Bad news from the Pentagon. Hackers spent nine months inside a defense file share, taking records on about three million people. Social Security numbers, unencrypted. And nobody knows who did it.

lines.speaker: kopi
lines.text: DeepSeek, with help from Huawei, open-sourced six AI tools for Ascend chips. Key libraries keep their Nvidia APIs, and the matrix kernels hit ninety-nine percent of peak.

lines.speaker: kopi
lines.text: In California, Governor Newsom vetoed a bill that would have banned secretly recording people with smart glasses and other wearables. He called it too broad, and said current law already covers it.

lines.speaker: kopi
lines.text: And for builders: Shopify launched Canvas. Just chat with its AI agent, Sidekick, and it edits your store's real theme code while you watch. It's rolling out over the next few days.

lines.speaker: kopi
lines.text: That's the diff for today. Now go build something, and happy Friday!
